title: FreeSWITCH SIP MESSAGE 'api' chat-proto command execution: now in CISA KEV (Nov 9)
why: No longer ahead: CISA added CVE-2026-116779 to KEV on Nov 9, 2026. SignalWire's advisory GHSA-mg63-h38w-8p9p had already reported exploitation in the wild.
action: Upgrade FreeSWITCH, and any PBX or contact-center product that bundles it, to 1.11.3. Until then set enable-chat=false on profiles that don't need it, and review logs for unexpected inbound SIP MESSAGE and API activity.
product: FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier (fixed in 1.11.3)

title: OpenSSH 'SSHole' password-auth bypass on musl/Alpine: now in CISA KEV (Nov 9), exploited in the wild
why: No longer ahead: CISA added CVE-2026-123158 to KEV on Nov 9, 2026. Before that, Previdian, GreyNoise, Defused, watchTowr and SANS ISC all reported exploitation, mostly by botnets and crypto miners.
action: Upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the fixed Alpine package and restart sshd. Until then set PasswordAuthentication no. Check logs for successful password logins to '*' accounts and for new authorized_keys entries.
product: OpenSSH sshd before 10.6p2 on musl-based Linux (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto) without PAM

title: Chrome XML use-after-free zero-day exploited in the wild (eighth Chrome 0-day of 2026)
why: Google said on Nov 9 that it is aware an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild (Chrome Releases; BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek, THN). SecurityWeek reports CISA has not added it to KEV, and no Microsoft Edge security release or MSRC entry for this CVE was seen yet (MSRC feed had no new items this run).
action: Force Chrome to 157.0.8103.50/.51 or later via your management tooling and relaunch browsers; watch for the Microsoft Edge security release that picks up CVE-2026-125350 and push it immediately.
product: Google Chrome before 157.0.8103.50 (Linux) / 157.0.8103.50/.51 (Windows, macOS); other Chromium browsers incl. Microsoft Edge until they ship the fix

title: Able2Shell: 33 unpatched N-able N-central zero-days with public PoC, incl. unauthenticated XXE-to-root RCE; N-able takes hosted N-central offline
why: Researcher Sean Bales published Python PoC code for 33 N-central flaws (GitHub 'Able2Shell') late Nov 8, including an anonymous XXE chain to code execution and admin creation. N-able confirmed critical vulnerabilities, took hosted N-central offline Nov 9 and told on-prem customers to shut servers down; hotfix expected around mid-day Nov 10 EST. No CVEs, not in CISA KEV; N-able reports no exploitation seen as of Nov 9.
action: Keep every on-prem N-central server offline (or fully off the internet) until N-able's Able2Shell hotfix is applied and N-able clears restart; review N-central logins, new admin accounts, scripts and Take Control sessions since Nov 8.
product: N-able N-central (on-premises appliance and hosted); tested on Appliance 2026.4.0.31, earlier releases believed affected; 2026.4 HF1 does not fix

title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQLi-to-root RCE: public Metasploit module, not in KEV
why: Rapid7's Metasploit release (Nov 6) adds an unauthenticated SQLi-to-root RCE module for Secure Email Gateway that Rapid7 believes maps to CVE-2026-76443. Sibling CVEs 76461 and 76519 are in KEV; 76443 itself is not in KEV and has no reported in-the-wild use.
action: Confirm every Secure Email Gateway/SEWM runs a fixed build (15.5.5-014 / 16.5.0-780 or later) and restrict management interfaces to trusted hosts.
product: Cisco Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (AsyncOS) 15.5 and earlier

affected.product: Cisco AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway

title: Zyxel GS1900 switches: zero-day used in attacks on ~1,000 switches bypasses the KEV-listed CVE-2026-7273 patch; new CVE-2026-107441 is not in KEV
why: Binarly recovered the attackers' 'GS1900 Pre-Auth RCE' exploit from Red Heron/JITTERLY infrastructure and showed that it still works without changes on all 10 Patch 2 builds that were released to fix KEV-listed CVE-2026-7273. GreyNoise had reported 996 switches looted around Aug 17. Zyxel shipped Patch 3 on Oct 22 and published the advisory on Nov 3 (BleepingComputer, THN, SecurityOnline). CISA's KEV catalog lists only the old CVE-2026-7273; THN notes CVE-2026-107441 is not in KEV. It is unclear how many of the 996 victims fell to the new bug, and the vendor does not confirm exploitation. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every GS1900 switch to the 2.90(.3)C0 firmware for its model, move the web management interface onto a management VLAN, and treat any exposed switch as compromised: rotate its root/admin passwords and review its configuration.
product: Zyxel GS1900 series switches (10 models) on firmware 2.90(xxxx.2)C0 and earlier, i.e. including the June 'Patch 2' fix for CVE-2026-7273; fixed in 2.90(xxxx.3)C0

title: DreamHost File Manager breach: an undisclosed third-party software flaw was exploited from Aug to Oct 23, exposing FTP/SFTP passwords and webmail sessions
why: DreamHost's breach notice (filed with the California AG; BleepingComputer, TechCrunch and gbhackers, Nov 4) says an attacker exploited a vulnerability in the third-party software behind its File Manager from about August 2026 until Oct 23. The attacker stole FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail credentials and session tokens. The software and the flaw have not been named, so other hosts running the same file manager cannot yet check themselves. No CVE, nothing in KEV, and not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: If you host sites on DreamHost, rotate FTP/SFTP and mailbox passwords (and any reused elsewhere), diff site files against a known-good copy for injected code, and remove unknown mailbox forwarding rules.
product: DreamHost web-based File Manager (files.dreamhost.com) and webmail; the exploited third-party File Manager software is unnamed

title: Control Web Panel: CWPdoor trojanized cwpsrv backdoor found on real servers, as public exploit for CWP2Shell root RCE chain lands
why: XLab (via BleepingComputer, Nov 5) found CWPdoor, a trojanized cwpsrv, with real victims; VulnCheck published a working go-exploit module for the CWP2Shell unauthenticated-to-root chain (disclosed Nov 2). None of these CVEs is in CISA KEV. How CWPdoor gets installed is unknown, and the CWP2Shell flaws have no confirmed in-the-wild use yet. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade CWP to the latest release (1.29+/1.30), restrict port 2083/2087/2031 to admin networks, and run XLab's triage checks for a trojanized cwpsrv (socket, process and binary-string checks listed in the BleepingComputer report); if positive, replace the binary and rotate all panel credentials.
product: Control Web Panel (CWP7) webpanel before 1.29 (CWP2Shell chain); cwpsrv binary replaced by CWPdoor on compromised hosts

title: LNbits Lightning wallet servers: unpatched exploit used to drain funds; project tells all operators to shut down
why: On Nov 8 the LNbits project said a 'wave of attacks' had hit its servers and told every operator to shut down. One operator (BitTipBot) lost 2,285,545 sats to newly created accounts between 09:22 and 14:00 UTC (THN, CoinInsider, news.bitcoin.com). There is no CVE, no fixed release (GitHub still showed v1.6.2 at 14:46 UTC Nov 9) and no CISA KEV entry.
action: Keep every LNbits instance stopped until the project releases the fixed version. Then check for unexpected new accounts and withdrawals since Nov 8, and rotate the funding-source (LND/CLN) credentials LNbits holds.
product: LNbits (self-hosted Lightning wallet/accounts server) up to v1.6.2, the latest release; Paywall extension flagged first

title: Web3Auth (Consensys) embedded-wallet flaw exposed Keplr social-login private keys; attacker drained wallets
why: Web3Auth and Keplr confirmed a flaw in Web3Auth's infrastructure that exposed private keys of social-login wallets, and that an 'original attacker' used it from Nov 6 (The Block, THN). GoPlus estimates at least $1M stolen. The flaw is in a hosted service: there is no CVE, no public technical detail and no CISA KEV entry.
action: If you or your app use Web3Auth embedded wallets or Keplr social login, stop sending funds to those addresses. Move liquid assets to a seed-phrase or hardware wallet, and follow only official Keplr/Web3Auth channels for recovery: scam 'recovery' offers are circulating.
product: Web3Auth embedded wallet service; Keplr wallets created with Google or Apple login

title: German web host mittwald breached via its MCP (AI-assistant) server: session tokens stolen, 56 customer projects compromised
why: mittwald disclosed (blog post Nov 7, The Record) that an attacker used a flaw in its MCP server from Oct 27 to Nov 4 to read customers' session tokens and compromise 56 projects. The flaw is in a hosted service: there is no CVE, no technical writeup yet (promised for next week) and no CISA KEV entry.
action: If you are a mittwald customer who used the MCP server after Oct 27, change passwords, enable 2FA, and delete unknown API and SSH keys. Rotate the database, mail and third-party credentials stored in your projects.
product: mittwald mStudio MCP server (AI assistant interface)

title: GPUStack loopback-trust auth bypass to admin and RCE, exploited in the wild: added to CISA KEV Nov 9
why: Not ahead: CISA added it to KEV on Nov 9, 2026. Advisory GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr reports exploitation in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment, reported by Javier Sixto of ulex.fr.
action: Upgrade GPUStack to 2.2.0 or later, or set force_auth_localhost=true and strip X-GPUStack-Real-IP at the proxy. Afterwards revoke unknown admin API keys and backends, and rotate worker and cloud credentials.
product: GPUStack before 2.2.0 (exploited against 2.1.1)

title: CPython sandbox-escape 0-day disclosed by RunSybil; upstream treated it as a bug, not a security issue
why: On Nov 5, oss-security relayed RunSybil's blog on a CPython sandbox escape. RunSybil could not get it handled as a security vulnerability, so it submitted fix PR #155761, and upstream is not backporting it to security releases. A downstream review (MaplePrivacyLabs PR #1409) mentions a RunSybil Jinja sandbox-escape demonstration and a CPython GenericAlias out-of-bounds read (cpython#155752) first guarded in 3.14.8. No CVE, no advisory, not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Don't treat Jinja SandboxedEnvironment or other in-process Python sandboxes as a security boundary for untrusted input. Isolate them in a container or VM, and move 3.14 runtimes to the latest 3.14.x.
product: CPython (affected versions unconfirmed; one downstream review cites a GenericAlias out-of-bounds read guarded from 3.14.8)

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB PRO refrigeration controllers hijacked into an SMTP botnet
why: SecurityScorecard STRIKE (OTX pulse, Nov 6) found a suspected SMTP botnet including confirmed XWEB PRO controllers, citing unpatched CVE-2026-25085. Not in CISA KEV; CISA SSVC still lists exploitation 'none'. CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT issued a joint fact sheet (Nov 5) on active targeting of refrigeration controllers; Censys saw a 53% drop in exposed Danfoss StoreView/XWEB controllers. The CVE is still not in KEV.
action: Take XWEB controllers off the public internet (VPN-only), update to the latest Copeland firmware, and check for unexpected outbound SMTP from OT networks.
product: XWEB 300D PRO / 500D PRO / 500B PRO firmware 1.12.1 and earlier

title: hyperglass looking glass: unauthenticated command injection in /api/query; 36 ISP/hosting hosts shown exploitable, upstream unpatched
why: Disclosed Nov 10 on oss-security and hyperpwn.xyz (research attributed to DeepSeek, validated by the poster): target strings are put into router/shell commands unescaped, and /api/query is unauthenticated by default. The write-up reports 36 internet-exposed instances across 20 ASNs with command execution (11 root or equivalent). Upstream issue open since July, no CVE, not in KEV.
action: Take internet-facing hyperglass instances offline or put them behind authentication/an allowlist, and restrict query types until a fixed release exists; rotate router/SSH credentials configured in hyperglass.
product: hyperglass upstream (fix PR #382 / issue #383 still open); hardened fork z23/hyperglass mitigates

title: Trojanized ARTEX AI pentest Docker image (tomicdd/artex) gives unauthenticated root shell; 62 exposed consoles; CERT-In flags Crafty Falcon
why: BadByte analysis (Nov 4) and The Hacker News (Nov 5) document a backdoor in a widely pulled ARTEX Docker image (~9,000 pulls, 62 internet consoles serving it Nov 2-4). No CVE, vendor advisory or CISA KEV entry exists (Ostorlab, Nov 5). Use of the backdoor against those consoles has not been reported. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Search container hosts and registries for tomicdd/artex or congdonglinux/artex; stop and preserve any such container, rebuild from reviewed source only, and rotate every secret the container could read.
product: tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex Docker images (backdoored copies of ARTEX v0.3.15)

title: DigiCert breach: internet-exposed archive system leaked customer contacts and some ID documents (passports, licences)
why: DigiCert breach notification and Mozilla Bugzilla incident report (BleepingComputer, Nov 5) confirm unauthorized read access to archived validation data via a self-registration flaw after a Feb 2025 migration. This is a vendor breach, not a patchable CVE: there is no KEV entry and nothing for Defender to detect. The main risk is phishing that impersonates certificate validation. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Identify which of your staff submitted organization/identity validation documents to DigiCert, warn them, and treat 're-upload your ID / validation failed' messages claiming to be DigiCert as phishing; no certificate reissue is needed.
product: DigiCert internal archived-customer-data business system (CA services, CertCentral, DigiCert ONE reported unaffected)

title: Chainalysis breach: 'offensive agentic' intrusion exposed password hashes and live tokens for all users; KYT/Reactor offline
why: In its Nov 4 update Chainalysis said names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users were exposed. It also reported an on-path attack that captured some passwords and some KYT accounts accessed without authorization. The Record, The Register, THN and American Banker all report it. The vulnerability and actor have not been disclosed, so there is nothing for KEV or Microsoft to track yet, and no detection guidance exists.
action: If your organization uses Chainalysis, rotate its API keys and passwords (and any reused elsewhere), revoke integrations that hold Chainalysis tokens, and review KYT/API activity since October for unauthorized use.
product: Chainalysis Reactor, KYT, Address Screening, Data Solutions (hosted)

title: InfiniteWP Client (WordPress, ~200k installs) NOSSL management key has 31 bits of secret; forged admin commands demonstrated
why: Researcher 'theknell' disclosed on oss-security (Nov 6) with a public write-up (GitHub the-knell/Thirty-One-Bits): the NOSSL signing key is MD5(panel public key + one rand()), recovered offline in 291.9 s from one captured request, and a forged state-changing command was accepted on their own instance. No CVE, vendor fix unverified, not in KEV; MSRC n/a.
action: On sites using InfiniteWP, check whether the client is enrolled in NOSSL mode; if so, deactivate/reactivate and re-add the site via the RSA (OpenSSL) path, or remove the plugin until a vendor fix ships.
product: InfiniteWP Client WordPress plugin 1.13.10 (sites enrolled in NOSSL mode)

title: Qubole's trusted AWS cross-account access abused to steal secrets, Entra ID/Okta client credentials and S3 data from customers
why: Wiz (with Sentra and Mandiant) published on Nov 9 that an attacker used Qubole-side IAM credentials Oct 14-26 to assume customer integration roles, harvest Lambda/Secrets Manager/SSM secrets (incl. Microsoft Entra ID client secrets) and copy S3 data. No vendor statement, no CVE, not in KEV, and no Microsoft advisory on the stolen Entra secrets.
action: Hunt CloudTrail from Oct 1 for AssumeRole from Qubole's AWS account originating outside AWS (per Wiz's guidance), delete unused Qubole roles, and rotate every secret, Entra ID app secret and Okta credential those roles could read.
product: Qubole data lake platform AWS integration roles (incl. dormant roles still trusting account 805246085872)

title: Malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases steal Swarm wallet keys and install backdoors
why: Ethersphere confirmed both releases were published by an attacker using its release identity/CI credentials on Nov 9 (GHSA-hh7j-5m3j-23pf / MAL-2026-18773). Socket, StepSecurity and SafeDep analysed the loader: wallet theft plus a backdoor (hidden ScreenConnect on Windows), C2 shared with the SleepyDuck campaign. No CVE, not in KEV.
action: Search lockfiles, caches and CI logs for @ethersphere/bee-js@13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2; pin bee-js 13.2.0 / install Desktop 0.56.3, rebuild any host that ran them and move Swarm node funds to a new key.
product: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 (npm, live ~75 min Nov 9) and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 (GitHub/auto-update, ~8.5 h)

title: Keycloak SAML HTTP-Redirect signature bypass (CVSS 9.1): unauthenticated takeover of federated accounts
why: Red Hat CVE published Nov 5 (CVSS 9.1, pre-auth); a Sploitus entry exists but no verified public exploit, and it is not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Apply the Red Hat/Keycloak fix for CVE-2026-117691; until then block SAML redirect-binding requests with percent-encoded SAMLResponse/SAMLRequest parameter names at the WAF and review SAML broker logins.
product: Keycloak / Red Hat build of Keycloak (SAML HTTP-Redirect binding); fixed versions not yet stated in our sources

title: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection in element search (admin takeover)
why: VulnCheck/GHSA advisory published Nov 6 for an unauthenticated stacked-query SQLi (CVSS 9.3/9.8); no exploit or in-the-wild use seen yet. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade Craft CMS to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2.

title: IBM API Connect mass disclosure: ~200 CVEs incl. unauthenticated RCE, auth bypass and hard-coded admin credentials
why: IBM published ~200 API Connect CVEs on Nov 7 (NVD/CVE.org), several unauthenticated 9.8s: path-traversal RCE (17340), OS command injection (17408), hard-coded admin credentials (17360/17403), signature-verification auth bypass (17301). No public exploit yet (VulDB); not in CISA KEV; non-Microsoft so MSRC n/a.
action: Inventory API Connect 10.0.8.x/12.1.x deployments, apply IBM's fix from the security bulletin, and restrict management/portal endpoints to trusted networks until patched.

title: SAP November 2026 Patch Day: 9 critical fixes, four CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated NetWeaver/Web Dispatcher/Gateway flaws
why: SAP published 38 CVEs on its Nov 10 Patch Day, including an unauthenticated SAML/assertion authentication bypass in AS ABAP (CVE-2026-120017), a high-privilege default Gateway ACL (CVE-2026-89103) and unauthenticated memory corruption in Web Dispatcher/AS ABAP (CVE-2026-89126, CVE-2026-76964). None is in CISA KEV and no exploitation is reported yet; SAP patch days are quickly targeted (SANS saw scanning for old NetWeaver webshells Nov 9).
action: Apply the November SAP Security Notes to internet-facing Web Dispatcher, Gateway and AS ABAP systems first; until patched, restrict Gateway/ICM/Web Dispatcher ports to trusted networks and review SAML2 settings on ABAP systems.
product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP / ABAP Platform, SAP Web Dispatcher, SAP Gateway, SAP Kernel, BusinessObjects BI (versions per SAP Security Notes)

title: Fireworks AI second breach via its cloud provider exposes customer data incl. Notion AI chat transcripts
why: Fireworks notified customers Nov 9 (Bloomberg, BleepingComputer) that an attacker pivoted from a breached third-party cloud provider to its development machines on Oct 24, touching tens of thousands of files with some customer data. Notion's advisory says Notion AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of workspaces were exposed. No CVE, not in KEV.
action: If you use Fireworks or Notion AI, check for breach notifications and rotate any credentials or API keys that were pasted into Notion AI or stored in Fireworks jobs since October.
product: Fireworks AI inference/fine-tuning platform (development machines); downstream Notion (<1% of workspaces), Cursor and others

title: Apache Axis 1.x (EOL) unauthenticated remote class instantiation via SOAP fault: no fix
why: Apache disclosed a critical, unauthenticated flaw on oss-security (Nov 6) in an unsupported library still embedded in many Java products; no released fix. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Inventory Java apps and appliances bundling axis-1.x jars and plan migration; restrict network access to SOAP endpoints that act as Axis 1.x clients/servers.
product: Apache Axis 1.x through 1.4 (end of life)

title: WorkOS breach: researcher's ARTEX AI agent used a leaked dev credential to pull customer CRM/support data
why: WorkOS's Nov 6 bulletin update (BleepingComputer, Nov 6) says an ARTEX agent run by a researcher reached an internet-exposed internal API with a predictable dev credential (Oct 25-30) and extracted customer records. This is an incident at a SaaS vendor, so there is no CVE, KEV entry or Microsoft advisory to cover it.
action: If you are a WorkOS customer, warn staff about phishing that cites real WorkOS support or sales conversations. Audit your own internal tools for internet exposure and leftover dev credentials.
product: WorkOS internal sales/customer-support tool (not the WorkOS auth product)

title: IBM Concert 1.0-3.0.1.1 unauthenticated OS command injection (CVE-2026-6715, CVE-2026-15266, CVSS 9.8)
why: IBM published two CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/PR:N) OS command injection CVEs, which NVD listed on Nov 8 (IBM advisory node 7294607). VulDB says no public exploit. Neither CVE is in CISA KEV.
action: Apply the fix in IBM advisory 7294607 and restrict network access to the Concert UI and API to admin networks.
product: IBM Concert 1.0 through 3.0.1.1

title: D-Link DGS-3130 switches: multiple unpatched DDP zero-days (no CVEs yet)
why: D-Link published mitigations (BleepingComputer, Nov 6) for unpatched D-Link Discovery Protocol flaws; no CVE, no patch, no exploitation reported. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Disable DDP, remove default SNMP communities, and restrict SSH/web/SNMP management to an isolated management network.
product: DGS-3130 series (DGS-3130-30TS, multiple firmware versions)

title: OpenAM (Open Identity Platform) unauthenticated session-token theft via notification WebSocket (CVSS 10.0), plus unsigned-SAML auth bypass and self-registration admin creation; fixed in 16.1.4
why: Vendor GHSA advisories and OpenAM 16.1.4 came out Oct 22; VulnCheck published the CVEs on Nov 8 (NVD items in this run, Ostorlab write-up). An unauthenticated attacker can hijack admin sessions. Missing on Microsoft's side: not in CISA KEV (Senserva KEV-7d list, Nov 7). Sploitus lists a VulnCheck 'PoC' entry, unverified. No exploitation reported.
action: Upgrade OpenAM to 16.1.4. Until then, restrict /openam/notifications and the Liberty ID-FF endpoints to policy-agent hosts, set WantAssertionsSigned=true, and disable self-registration. After upgrading, review sessions and admin accounts on instances that faced the internet.
product: OpenAM before 16.1.4 (token disclosure: 14.0.0 through 16.1.3)
